blocks.title: Equation of continuity
blocks.text: Pipe ke kisi bhi point par pipe ke cross-sectional area aur fluid ki speed ka product (multiply karne ka jawab, yani Av) constant rehta hai. Yeh constant har second mein behne wale fluid ka volume hai, yani seedha flow rate.
Ek aisa pipe lein jis ki motai har jagah barabar nahi (non-uniform). Steady flow mein fluid ke particles ek hi lines par chalte hain (Fig. 5.15).

blocks.alt: Mura hua tube neeche ke sire (area A1) se oopar ke chaure sire (area A2) tak uthta hai. Neeche ke sire mein lambai delta x1 ki rangeen tukri aur oopar ke sire mein chhoti lambai delta x2 ki rangeen tukri hai. Teer v1 aur v2 neeche se andar aur oopar se bahar flow (behna) dikhate hain.
blocks.caption: Figure 5.15: Fluid ka steady flow (waqt ke saath na badalne wala flow) (kitab ki Figure 5.15 ke mutabiq original drawing).

blocks.title: Diagram ko samjhein
blocks.text: Dono shaded hisson se ek hi time Δt mein fluid ka barabar mass guzarta hai. Neeche wala sira patla hai, is liye wahan shaded hissa lamba (Δx₁ bara) aur speed v₁ zyada hai; oopar wala sira mota hai, hissa chhota aur speed kam: A₁v₁ = A₂v₂.
Ek chhote time Δt mein tube ke neeche wale sire par fluid velocity v₁ se faasla Δx₁ tay karta hai:

blocks.title: Interesting Fact
blocks.text: Euler ne 1752 mein incompressible fluid ke liye continuity equation hasil ki thi, jis mein bohat si terms thin. Kitab ke mutabiq baad mein 1954 mein C. Truesdell ne is ka English se tarjuma kiya.
Agar neeche wale sire ka cross-sectional area A₁ ho to A₁ se tube mein dakhil hone wale fluid ka volume:
Agar fluid ki density ρ₁ ho to shaded hisse (A₁ wale) mein fluid ka mass:
Isi tarah usi time Δt mein oopar wale sire (area A₂) se velocity v₂ se nikalne wale fluid ka mass:
Yahan ρ₂ A₂ se nikalne wale fluid ki density hai, aur Δm chhota sa mass hai.

Agar fluid incompressible ho aur flow steady ho to fluid ka mass conserve hota hai (na banta hai na khatam hota hai): time Δt mein A₁ se andar aane wala mass usi time mein A₂ se bahar jane wale mass ke barabar hona chahiye. Is liye:

blocks.latex: A_1 v_1 \Delta t \times \rho_1 = A_2 v_2 \Delta t \times \rho_2

blocks.text: Equation (5.17) ko equation of continuity kehte hain. Incompressible fluid ke steady flow mein density constant hai (ρ₁ = ρ₂), is liye equation ban jati hai:
Equation (5.18) kehti hai ke steady flow mein andar aane ka rate of flow bahar jane ke rate of flow ke barabar hai.
Yeh equation pipe mein behte fluid ke mass ke conservation (mass ka qaim rehna) ko sabit karti hai.

blocks.title: Example 5.4
blocks.problem: Pani ke hose (pipe) ka outlet par andar ka diameter 20 mm hai, aur yeh 60 s mein 30 kg pani nikalta hai. Outlet par pani ki speed nikalein. Pani ki density 1000 kg m⁻³ aur flow steady maan lein.
steps: Diameter D = 20 mm = 0.02 m, radius r = D/2 = 0.01 m
Har second mein mass = m/t = 30 kg / 60 s = 0.5 kg s⁻¹
Continuity se har second nikalne wala mass = ρAv, is liye v = (mass per second) / (ρA)

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ne aakhri jawab “0.6 m” chhapa hai. Magar 0.5 × 10 / 3.14 = 1.59, yani taqreeban 1.6, aur speed ka unit m s⁻¹ hai, sirf m nahi. Sahi jawab v ≈ 1.6 m s⁻¹ hai.

blocks.title: Tidbits
blocks.text: Nal se girta pani neeche aate hue tez hota jata hai, is liye continuity equation (A₁v₁ = A₂v₂) ke mutabiq us ki dhaar patli hoti jati hai.

blocks.title: For Your Information
blocks.text:
Equation of continuity in jagahon par lagu hoti hai:
(i) arteries aur veins (khoon ki nasoon) mein khoon ka flow
(ii) daryaon aur pipes mein pani ka flow
(iii) ducts aur ventilation systems mein hawa ka flow.

blocks.prompt: 0.05 m diameter ke pipe mein pani 2 m s⁻¹ se beh raha hai; aage pipe ka diameter 0.03 m reh jata hai. Patle hisse mein velocity nikalein. Yeh equation mass ke conservation ki shakal kyun hai?
blocks.explanation: A₁v₁ = A₂v₂ aur A = πd²/4, is liye v₂ = v₁ (d₁/d₂)² = 2 × (0.05/0.03)² = 2 × 2.78 ≈ 5.56 m s⁻¹. Yeh mass ke conservation ki shakal is liye hai ke yeh har second andar aane wale mass ko bahar jane wale mass ke barabar rakhti hai: steady flow mein incompressible fluid ka pipe ke andar na mass jama hota hai na ghaib hota hai.

items: Δt mein andar ka mass = bahar ka mass: A₁v₁ρ₁ = A₂v₂ρ₂ (5.17); incompressible fluid: A₁v₁ = A₂v₂ (5.18); yeh mass ka conservation hai.
Patle hisse mein speed zyada, mote hisse mein kam.
Example 5.4: v = 0.5 kg s⁻¹ / (1000 × 3.14 × 10⁻⁴) ≈ 1.6 m s⁻¹ (kitab mein ghalti se 0.6 m).
